findings.title: Cache key uses non-deterministic hash()
findings.body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. CPython randomizes the hash seed for tuples/strings per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project set produces a different key in every web/worker process. The 60s cache therefore never shares data across processes, defeating the stated 'performance optimization during traffic spikes'. The PR description claims this cache avoids 'expensive repeated option lookups during high-traffic periods', but with N workers you still get N independent option lookups. Replace `hash(...)` with a deterministic digest (e.g. `hashlib.md5(str(tuple(sorted(project_ids))).encode()).hexdigest()`) or just stringify the tuple.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined and documented as 'This should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency', but nothing in the PR (or elsewhere in the diff) ever calls it. With the 60s TTL, removing a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` will continue to return stale `is_eligible=True` results for up to a minute, meaning queries against that org/project will keep being rewritten to `upsampled_count()` even after the operator un-allowlisted it. Either wire up invalidation on option writes, or remove the unused helper to avoid implying a guarantee that isn't there.

findings.title: Error-sampling context silently overwrites an existing sample_rate
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` runs unconditionally during `store_event` and writes `normalized_data['sample_rate'] = float(client_sample_rate)` whenever `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` is truthy, without checking whether `sample_rate` was already set. Any pre-existing `sample_rate` (e.g. set by ingest earlier in the pipeline, by a different sampling decision, or by a test fixture) is silently overwritten. The bare `except Exception` blocks also swallow any unexpected type of `contexts` value, hiding malformed payloads. The function should at most set `sample_rate` if it is currently missing, and should not catch arbitrary `Exception`.

findings.title: Repeated lazy imports inside hot helper
findings.body: `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` performs `from sentry.snuba import discover, errors` and later `from sentry.snuba import transactions` inside the function body on every call. Even with module caching this is avoidable per-call dict lookups, and it is invoked from the timeseries hot path of every organization events stats request. If the lazy style is only to dodge a circular import, move both imports to module scope in one statement and resolve the cycle properly.

findings.title: Comments around upsampling block are misleading
findings.body: The newly added comments in `_get_event_stats` make claims that don't match the code: 'Early upsampling eligibility check for performance optimization ... This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution' (it isn't actually cached at the call site, and the helper's cache is broken by the hash() issue), and 'Apply upsampling transformation just before query execution ... This late transformation ensures we use the most current schema assumptions' (schema does not change at runtime, and the transformation isn't late in any meaningful sense — it runs before every branch). These comments will mislead future readers about what the code does and why; either justify the comments accurately or remove them.

findings.title: Upsampling check runs unconditionally on every stats request
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` is invoked unconditionally on every `_get_event_stats` call, including for non-error datasets and for projects that are not allowlisted (the common case). Even with a hot cache this still does a cache key construction (with the broken `hash()`), a cache get, and a dataset/parse check per call. Move the check inside the branches where `final_columns` is actually used, or short-circuit cheaply on dataset (transactions/spans/metrics) before touching the cache.
